title: Multi-species engine-convection feasibility spike (Bridge B / B1.x)
conclusion: FEASIBLE (YES). A synthetic TWO-species axial graph (parent liver__ax1..N + metabolite__ax1..N + shared metabolite_sink) compiles and solves on the stock engine with ZERO src/engine change: T1 compiles, T2 solves, T3 mass-conserves (mass_balance_error 3.55e-15; species balance closes, formed 52.47 = chain_end 3.378e-17 + sink_end 52.47). T4: per-zone formation is spatially resolved and inter-zone convection (TransitEdge) moves the metabolite center-of-mass toward the outlet. T5: a Damkohler sweep (Da = N*k_detox/k_conv, k_conv fixed) shows the convection-vs-local shift is large at low Da (convected/stable regime) and ~0 at high Da (local/reactive regime); monotone-decreasing = True. Production already ships well-mixed multi-species, so this validates AXIAL composition; the high-Da agreement (shift->0) validates the local-only post-processor (scripts/probe_zonal_hazard.py) as the Da>>1 limit. Harness-isolated; headline 2.731 bit-identical.
